title: Consumption Onramp Accelerator and Fidelity Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
summary: A pragmatic, step-by-step playbook to accelerate customer consumption onramp while preserving output fidelity and predictable unit economics. Targets self-serve developers and early-stage PLG accounts transitioning to production usage.
background: Teams adopting Redwood often face three simultaneous friction points: unclear fidelity defaults across environments, surprise token costs when usage scales, and brittle rollout paths between hosted/dedicated/private. This playbook captures recommended presets, integration checklists, and a phased onboarding path that aligns fidelity, telemetry, and pricing nudges to reduce churn and speed time-to-first-value.
goals: Reduce time-to-first-successful-call to < 15 minutes for a typical SDK user
Ensure default consumption path achieves >=95% fidelity for conversational flows used in the onboarding prompt set
Lower first-month cost surprises by providing predictive cost guidance and a soft spend cap
Provide safe, reversible fidelity rollouts for teams moving from hosted to dedicated/private deployments
scope: Applies to Redwood hosted API v2, Dedicated onboarding flows, and the Private onramp kit. Does not replace vertical-specific compliance onboarding (finance/healthcare) which remains separate. Covers developer UX, telemetry SLOs, default fidelity presets, and packaging recommendations for Starter and Growth tiers.
personas: ML/infra engineer (evaluates fidelity and cost tradeoffs)
Product ops / Solutions engineer (runs canaries and helps with Dedicated/private setup)
prerequisites: Customer account with Redwood and API key provisioned
Access to Redwood Console for telemetry and billing (role: org-admin or devops)
Representative prompt set (3–10 prompts) annotated with expected fidelity thresholds
Minimum observability: token-level metering enabled and session traces active
integration_checklist: Step 1: Create API key in Console -> API Keys. Scope: tokens:read, inference:invoke
Step 2: Install SDK (npm or pip) and run sample quickstart. Command: npm i @redwood/inference && node examples/quickstart.js
Step 3: Configure default fidelity preset (see 'Fidelity presets' below) in request headers: X-Redwood-Fidelity: balanced
Step 4: Enable telemetry ingestion: add X-Trace-ID header and forward traces to Redwood ingestion endpoint (HTTP/1.1) for first 14 days
Step 5: Set soft spend cap via Console -> Billing -> Alerts: 50% of expected first-month spend
Step 6: If moving to Dedicated, run the compatibility check script provided in the Private onramp kit and schedule a canary window with SRE
fidelity_presets_table:
| Preset | Intended use | Model variant | Default max_tokens | Latency target (p50) | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| conservative | Sensitive outputs, high-accuracy requirements | rdx-verified-1.2 | 512 | 120ms | Avoid quantized fallbacks; higher unit cost |
| balanced | Typical conversational/assistant flows (onboarding) | rdx-balanced-1.0 | 256 | 90ms | Default for Self-Serve & Starter bundle |
| economical | High-throughput, low-cost embeddings/chat snippets | rdx-econ-0.9 | 128 | 60ms | Aggressive quantization allowed; expect occasional fidelity variance |
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 — Pre-onboard (internal):
1) Create onboarding prompts (3–10) and expected output examples.
2) Run tests locally vs rdx-balanced-1.0 and rdx-econ-0.9; capture BLEU/ROUGE-like or task-specific metric.

Phase 1 — Self-serve roll (days 0–7):
1) Expose 'balanced' preset as default in quickstart SDK and Console.
2) Send welcome email with link to 15-min quickstart guide and embedded cost estimator.
3) Monitor: successful-call-rate (>90%), average cost-per-call, and onboarding retention metric (day 7 active).

Phase 2 — Guided onboarding (days 7–30):
1) Solutions engineer runs fidelity sweep using customer's annotated prompt set.
2) If fidelity < 95% for critical prompts, change recommended preset to 'conservative' and open a ticket with Research.
3) Offer a one-time 'Starter credit' and recommended warm capacity suggestion for bursty workloads.

Phase 3 — Production transition (after day 30):
1) Recommend Dedicated template if steady-state QPS > 50 and avg latency-sensitive routes require 99th percentile guarantees.
2) Run a 72-hour canary with traffic split 5% production -> Dedicated variant.
3) Validate telemetry: cost delta within expected band (+/- 15%), fidelity regressions = 0 for prioritized prompts.

Rollback guidance: revert traffic split to hosted within 30 minutes if error rate or fidelity regressions breach thresholds.
telemetry_and_slos:
Key signals to instrument during onboarding:
- Success metrics: successful_call_rate (goal >= 0.95), median_latency_ms (goal <= preset latency target), tokens_per_call
- Quality metrics: promptset_pass_rate (fraction of annotated prompts meeting expected fidelity), semantic_similarity (optional)
- Financial metrics: projected_monthly_spend, spend_alert_triggered (boolean)

Recommended SLOs for Starter package:
- Availability: 99.9% (monthly)
- Median latency (balanced): <= 90ms
- Promptset pass rate: >= 95% for critical prompts
- Spend-notification: first alert at 50% of configured monthly threshold
pricing_and_packaging_recommendations:
Starter bundle (target SMB/devs):
- Includes: 100k tokens free trial + onboarding credits (USD 500) + Console quickstart
- Default fidelity: balanced
- Soft spend cap: 50% of expected monthly billing; one-click uplift available

Growth bundle (target scale-up teams):
- Reserved warm capacity recommendation with 10% discount; telemetry retention extended to 90 days
- Add-on: fidelity consultation (one hour) and canary run support

Commercial notes: clearly display median token cost per preset in Console and in the quickstart cost estimator. When switching presets in Console, show a projected % cost delta and expected fidelity delta based on historical lab runs.
migration_and_rollback: Always run a fidelity sweep against the customer's annotated prompt set prior to migration
Start with split traffic: 95% hosted / 5% Dedicated for 72 hours, monitor the three highest-priority prompts continuously
If promptset_pass_rate drops by >3 percentage points for any priority prompt, pause migration and open a regression ticket
Automated rollback: traffic manager should support a single-step revert and notify owners; target revert time < 30 minutes
faq:
Q: What if a customer's prompts are highly domain-specific?
A: Use the conservative preset for initial production traffic and schedule a fidelity tuning session with Research; consider a variant adapter if a private model is required.

Q: How do we estimate customer spend for the first month?
A: Use the Quickstart cost estimator in Console which multiplies expected calls/day * median tokens_per_call (based on preset) * token_price(preset). Provide scenario projections (low/medium/high).

Q: Can customers opt out of telemetry?
A: Core onboarding requires minimal telemetry (token-level metering and traces). For sensitive customers, use Private deployment with agreed audit logging levels; coordinate with Security and Legal.
